t: Universal Extraction Pipeline: a plain-language overview

t: How the Universal Extraction Pipeline works
title: How the Universal Extraction Pipeline works
description: Overview: what the Universal Extraction Pipeline does and why archives need it. Real pipelines start with content sniffing (magic numbers, MIME detection via libmagic) rather than trusting file extensions, then dispatch through a registry that maps detected types to extractor plugins — text extractors for documents, OCR for images, ASR for audio, parsers for structured data. Each stage is wrapped in timeouts and error handling so one corrupt file cannot stall the line; failures go to a quarantine queue with their error attached. Extracted content flows into a common record format with provenance noting which plugin handled each file.
demo:
# Universal Extraction Pipeline - runnable demo (JAH-ATK160-000002)
RANK = 2
SIG = False
SAMPLE = [('n.txt', 'plain notes'), ('m.json', '{"x": [1,2]}'), ('z.dat', 'ÿþ')]  # (filename, first_bytes_text)
def sniff(name, head):
    if head.startswith("{"): return "application/json"
    if head.startswith("<"): return "text/html"
    if "," in head.split("\n")[0] and "\n" in head: return "text/csv"
    if name.endswith(".txt"): return "text/plain"
    return "application/octet-stream"
def extract_text(mime, head):
    if mime == "application/json": return "json keys parsed"
    if mime == "text/html": return "html text stripped"
    if mime == "text/csv": return "csv rows parsed"
    if mime == "text/plain": return "plain text kept"
    return None
quarantine = []
for name, head in SAMPLE:
    mime = sniff(name, head)
    out = extract_text(mime, head)
    if out is None:
        quarantine.append((name, mime)); print("%-18s %-22s -> QUARANTINE" % (name, mime))
    else:
        print("%-18s %-22s -> %s" % (name, mime, out))
if RANK >= 2:
    print("routed:", len(SAMPLE)-len(quarantine), "| quarantined:", len(quarantine))
if RANK >= 3:
    from collections import Counter
    print("mime histogram:", dict(Counter(sniff(n, h) for n, h in SAMPLE)))
if SIG:
    print("Signature lineage stamp: JAH-SIG-PIPE-" + "JAH-ATK160-000002")
print("record:", "JAH-ATK160-000002", "OK")

t: How the Universal Extraction Pipeline works: the deep tour
title: How the Universal Extraction Pipeline works: the deep tour
description: Overview: what the Universal Extraction Pipeline does and why archives need it. Real pipelines start with content sniffing (magic numbers, MIME detection via libmagic) rather than trusting file extensions, then dispatch through a registry that maps detected types to extractor plugins — text extractors for documents, OCR for images, ASR for audio, parsers for structured data. Each stage is wrapped in timeouts and error handling so one corrupt file cannot stall the line; failures go to a quarantine queue with their error attached. Extracted content flows into a common record format with provenance noting which plugin handled each file. Production pipelines add priority lanes for large files, parallel workers with backpressure, and exactly-once bookkeeping so a crashed worker's files are re-queued rather than lost or duplicated. Routing rules are versioned and tested against a fixture corpus of every supported format. The limits are formats nobody has written an extractor for and adversarial files crafted to crash parsers — both are caught by the quarantine path, which preserves the raw file for later rather than discarding it.

t: The Universal Extraction Pipeline in production
title: The Universal Extraction Pipeline in production
description: Production: how the Universal Extraction Pipeline runs at archive scale and plugs into the extraction pipeline. Real pipelines start with content sniffing (magic numbers, MIME detection via libmagic) rather than trusting file extensions, then dispatch through a registry that maps detected types to extractor plugins — text extractors for documents, OCR for images, ASR for audio, parsers for structured data. Each stage is wrapped in timeouts and error handling so one corrupt file cannot stall the line; failures go to a quarantine queue with their error attached. Extracted content flows into a common record format with provenance noting which plugin handled each file.
demo:
# Universal Extraction Pipeline - runnable demo (JAH-ATK160-000014)
RANK = 2
SIG = False
SAMPLE = [('n.txt', 'plain notes'), ('m.json', '{"x": [1,2]}'), ('z.dat', 'ÿþ')]  # (filename, first_bytes_text)
def sniff(name, head):
    if head.startswith("{"): return "application/json"
    if head.startswith("<"): return "text/html"
    if "," in head.split("\n")[0] and "\n" in head: return "text/csv"
    if name.endswith(".txt"): return "text/plain"
    return "application/octet-stream"
def extract_text(mime, head):
    if mime == "application/json": return "json keys parsed"
    if mime == "text/html": return "html text stripped"
    if mime == "text/csv": return "csv rows parsed"
    if mime == "text/plain": return "plain text kept"
    return None
quarantine = []
for name, head in SAMPLE:
    mime = sniff(name, head)
    out = extract_text(mime, head)
    if out is None:
        quarantine.append((name, mime)); print("%-18s %-22s -> QUARANTINE" % (name, mime))
    else:
        print("%-18s %-22s -> %s" % (name, mime, out))
if RANK >= 2:
    print("routed:", len(SAMPLE)-len(quarantine), "| quarantined:", len(quarantine))
if RANK >= 3:
    from collections import Counter
    print("mime histogram:", dict(Counter(sniff(n, h) for n, h in SAMPLE)))
if SIG:
    print("Signature lineage stamp: JAH-SIG-PIPE-" + "JAH-ATK160-000014")
print("record:", "JAH-ATK160-000014", "OK")

description: Production: how the Universal Extraction Pipeline runs at archive scale and plugs into the extraction pipeline. Real pipelines start with content sniffing (magic numbers, MIME detection via libmagic) rather than trusting file extensions, then dispatch through a registry that maps detected types to extractor plugins — text extractors for documents, OCR for images, ASR for audio, parsers for structured data. Each stage is wrapped in timeouts and error handling so one corrupt file cannot stall the line; failures go to a quarantine queue with their error attached. Extracted content flows into a common record format with provenance noting which plugin handled each file. Production pipelines add priority lanes for large files, parallel workers with backpressure, and exactly-once bookkeeping so a crashed worker's files are re-queued rather than lost or duplicated. Routing rules are versioned and tested against a fixture corpus of every supported format. The limits are formats nobody has written an extractor for and adversarial files crafted to crash parsers — both are caught by the quarantine path, which preserves the raw file for later rather than discarding it.
